interpretations.interpretation_text: Across the 6 sampled frames (0s-222s), the modulation shape-editor pad shows six DIFFERENT hand-drawn curves in sequence (blank -> heart -> double-hump -> zigzag -> circle -> triangle). This is strong, genuinely visual evidence that the tutorial is demonstrating custom LFO/modulation shape drawing in Serum 2 — a technique used instead of a standard preset LFO shape. AMBIGUOUS: the exact modulation destination (which parameter this shape controls) is not legible at the source storyboard resolution (320x180) — no destination/routing label could be read. The mapping below to 'filter-cutoff' is inferred from genre convention (the video's own title, independently verified via yt-dlp metadata, is 'How to Make Dubstep GROWLS in SERUM 2 Tutorial' — dubstep growl-bass sound design conventionally uses a custom-drawn LFO shape to modulate filter cutoff), NOT a directly-read on-screen value. Note: Serum's target-parameter system does have a matching LFO.Shape capability target, but no CapabilityContract for it exists in this codebase yet, so it cannot be safely routed to execution — filter-cutoff is used instead as the closest EXISTING, contract-verified, admissible concept.
